blocks.explanation:
Yeh bilkul Question 6 jaisa hai, sirf libaas badla hai. Root ko power mein badla ja sakta hai: \(\sqrt[k]{x} = x^{\frac1k}\), yani square root power \(\frac12\), 4th root power \(\frac14\), waghera.
16, 64, 256 sab 4 ki powers hain (\(4^2, 4^3, 4^4\)), is liye poora product \(4^S\) ban jayega.
Plan: roots ko powers banao, sab ko 4 ki power mein likho, \(S\) nikalo, phir \(4^S\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\sqrt{4} \cdot \sqrt[4]{16} \cdot \sqrt[8]{64} \cdot \sqrt[16]{256} \cdots\)
Humein find karna hai: saabit karna hai ke product 16 hai.
Tareeqa: \(\sqrt[k]{x} = x^{\frac1k}\), indices ke qawaneen, aur powers ke jama ke liye A.G.P. ka tareeqa.

Roots ko powers mein badlein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 4^{\frac12} \cdot 16^{\frac14} \cdot 64^{\frac18} \cdot 256^{\frac{1}{16}} \cdots\]
Kyun: Square root ka matlab power \(\frac12\), 4th root ka matlab power \(\frac14\), 8th root \(\frac18\), aur 16th root \(\frac{1}{16}\).

Har base ko 4 ki power banayein
\[16 = 4^{2},\ 64 = 4^{3},\ 256 = 4^{4}\]
\[= 4^{\frac12} (4^{2})^{\frac14}\]
\[\quad \times (4^{3})^{\frac18} (4^{4})^{\frac{1}{16}} \cdots\]
\[= 4^{\frac12 + \frac24 + \frac38 + \frac{4}{16} + \cdots}\]
\[= 4^{S}\]
Kyun: \((4^2)^{\frac14} = 4^{\frac24}\), \((4^3)^{\frac18} = 4^{\frac38}\). Same base 4 ki powers multiply ho rahi hain, is liye powers jama: product \(4^S\) ban gaya. Ghaur karein ke \(S\) bilkul wahi series hai jo Question 6 mein thi.

Powers ka sum (infinite A.G.P.)
\[S = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{4}{16} + \cdots\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{2}{8} + \dfrac{3}{16} + \cdots\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{8} + \cdots\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}}{1 - \frac{1}{2}} = 1\]
\[S = 2\]
Kyun: Powers \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{2}{4}, \frac{3}{8}, \ldots\) ke upar \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\) (A.P.) aur neeche \(2, 4, 8, \ldots\) (G.P., \(r = \frac12\)) hain. Yani yeh khud ek infinite A.G.P. hai! \(\frac12\) se multiply, shift aur minus: har jore se upar sirf 1 bachta hai, jaise \(\frac{2 - 1}{4} = \frac14\). Jo bacha woh infinite G.P. hai: pehla term \(\frac12\), ratio \(\frac12\), sum \(\frac{1/2}{1/2} = 1\). Is liye \(\frac12 S = 1\) aur \(S = 2\).

Product hisaab karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 4^{S} = 4^{2} = 16 = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: \(S = 2\) rakha to \(4^2 = 16\), jo right side hai. Agar base 2 lete to powers \(1, 1, \frac34, \ldots\) aati aur \(2^4 = 16\) milta; jawab wahi, lekin base 4 se kaam chhota hai.
